description: Authored English search-intent cases for the twenty-two-mode Fluid Search demo; not user data. Two cases per mode in each disjoint split. Includes explicit negation, topic mentions and ambiguity. Separate from historical search-v1/search-v2 reports and archived composer datasets.

cases.draft: What is the history of tic-tac-toe?
cases.rationale: Mentioning a game in a history question does not request a playable board.

cases.draft: Don't start a timer; explain how a mechanical clock keeps time.
cases.rationale: The requested action is an explanation, and the timer is explicitly negated.
Practical rain planning implies a forecast without a command word.
The time qualifies a weather forecast, not publication filtering.
A ticker and share-price request imply a market quote.
Current market pricing is finance, not generic news.
The user wants physical nearby places.
Opening hours belong to local place discovery.
A film screening query belongs to movies.

cases.draft: family films in cinemas this weekend
cases.rationale: The weekend qualifies cinema availability rather than publication dates.
A quantity and target unit imply conversion.
Changing a monetary amount between currencies is conversion, not a stock quote.
The user asks for a word meaning.
A short phrase translation belongs to dictionary controls.
An explicit PDF target requests a document search.
A downloadable spreadsheet is a document-format search.
The query restricts results to a particular website.

cases.draft: search only NASA website for moon missions
cases.rationale: Source restriction is the primary refinement.
The user wants recent headlines.
Recent developments are a news search.
This filters reports by date without requesting a downloadable format.
The main refinement is a publication date range.

cases.draft: Find pages containing this exact phrase: a room of ones own
cases.rationale: The user requests an exact phrase match.

cases.draft: jaguar animal results without the car company
cases.rationale: Excluding an unwanted meaning is the requested refinement.
The user asks for numerical arithmetic, with no unit conversion.

cases.draft: Split $96 between 4 people with a 12% tip
cases.rationale: A bill split and percentage tip are local calculator operations.
A fixed countdown duration requests the timer rather than elapsed-time measurement.

cases.draft: Count down 45 seconds for my plank
cases.rationale: The user explicitly wants time to count down from a specified duration.

cases.draft: Start a stopwatch for my run
cases.rationale: The user requests a count-up stopwatch without a countdown duration.

cases.draft: Count up while I solve this puzzle
cases.rationale: Measuring elapsed time is a stopwatch task.
An explicit metronome and tempo request belongs to the beat tool.

cases.draft: Give me a steady 110 beats per minute for piano practice
cases.rationale: A regular musical practice pulse is a metronome, not a countdown.

cases.draft: Open a color picker for teal
cases.rationale: The user requests an editable colour picker for a supported named colour.
Inspecting a valid hex colour belongs to the colour tool.

cases.draft: Compare Earth and Mars side by side
cases.rationale: The explicit comparison of the supported planet pair requests the comparison tool.

cases.draft: How do Earth and Mars differ in day length and moons?
cases.rationale: The user asks for differences between two planets rather than an orbit simulation.

cases.draft: Let me simulate a satellite orbiting Earth
cases.rationale: The user requests an interactive gravitational orbit simulation.

cases.draft: Show an interactive model of how gravity changes an orbit
cases.rationale: The requested interactive model matches the prebuilt orbit tool.
The user asks to play the supported game rather than learn its history or rules.

cases.draft: Start a game of noughts and crosses
cases.rationale: Noughts and crosses is the supported tic-tac-toe game.
This explicitly requests the bounded visual Easter egg.

cases.draft: Make this little search window askew
cases.rationale: The user requests a visual tilt rather than a definition of askew.
The visitor requests the jumping dinosaur game or its explicit 404 Easter egg.
The visitor requests the jumping dinosaur game or its explicit 404 Easter egg.
